complexity_scope.guarantee: Zero success under the Gaussian prior for q<k; almost-sure recovery with k probes. This local claim is stronger than a 2/3 distributional obstruction and does not use a 2/3 assumption.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Exact integer threshold k; no asymptotic hidden constant.
complexity_scope.oracle: v maps to Av; A=A^T, so either allowed direction gives one such product.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Rank-k orthogonal P, exact equation A(I−P)=0; equivalent to relative-error success because OPT=0.
complexity_scope.resource: Individual exact products under a uniform cap; free internal linear algebra.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Lower: all measurable randomized adaptive matvec algorithms. Upper on rank-k PSD inputs: independent Gaussian probes.

content.intended_use: Separate zero-tail exact recovery from approximate full-rank hardness.

dependencies: Source s1: Lemma 4.1 conditional factorization; full statement and proof read, not independently re-proved here.
proofs.full_local_argument: Use Lemma 4.1 as an explicitly imported interface: for s=k and q≤k, orthogonalized informative queries yield, conditional on almost every actual transcript, a row-coordinate factor [B_q 0; C_q D_q], B_q invertible, B_q,C_q transcript-measurable, D_q an independent (d−q)×(k−q) iid N(0,1/d) block. Its latent right rotation preserves the column range. Dependent queries add no information; a shorter informative transcript may be extended and ignored. Fix the private seed, and first suppose 1≤q<k. Define T_q(x,y)=y−C_q B_q^(−1)x. Its kernel is the exposed range of [B_q;C_q], and T_q(range(G))=range(D_q). If A(I−P)=0, then range(I−P) is contained in ker(A); both have dimension d−k, so they are equal. Orthogonal complements give range(P)=range(A)=range(G). Conditional on the transcript, T_q(range(P)) is fixed. Equality would force it to be range(D_q). Since 1≤k−q<d−q, this Gaussian column space has nonatomic Haar law on Gr(k−q,d−q); the conditional equality probability is zero, including when the fixed subspace has the wrong dimension. Integrate over transcripts. For q=0 the same argument uses the nonatomic Haar law of range(G) itself. Integrating over the independent seed proves the randomized statement. Rank(A)=k almost surely implies OPT=0, so all finite-epsilon relative-error successes require the exact equation. For the upper witness, take Omega with k independent standard Gaussian columns. Conditional on every full-column-rank G, the columns of G^T Omega are independent nondegenerate Gaussian vectors in R^k; their square matrix is invertible almost surely. Therefore A Omega=G(G^T Omega) spans range(G), and its rank-k orthogonal projector satisfies A(I−P)=0 using exactly k products. These arguments establish both claims relative to the imported Lemma 4.1 interface.

assumptions: The same A is used throughout; the algorithm's private seed is independent of G.
Exact measurable adaptive matvec access; symmetric A makes transpose products equivalent. Each product costs one; internal computation and storage are uncharged.
The lower bound concerns a uniform cap q<k, not an expected query budget.
statement.conclusion: Exact range recovery on this family has k-query complexity under fixed positive success probability. Relative-error Schatten LRA inherits a k-query lower bound because success requires A(I−P)=0. This alone does not yield an accuracy-dependent lower bound for general inputs.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Integers 1≤k<d. G in R^{d×k}, G_ij iid N(0,1/d), A=GG^T. P is a transcript-measurable rank-k orthogonal projector. A has rank exactly k almost surely, so OPT_{p,k}(A)=0 for every 1≤p≤infinity.
statement.parameter_domains: 1≤k<d; arbitrary epsilon>0 and 1≤p≤infinity for the relative-error consequence.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every randomized adaptive algorithm capped at q<k, probability over G and its independent seed of A(I−P)=0 is zero. Thus any fixed positive distributional success probability requires at least k products; in particular any algorithm successful with positive fixed probability on every input requires k in the worst case. Conversely k independent Gaussian probes, independent of A, recover its range almost surely.
